messages:
maya: quick recap — ran INT6/INT8 priming sweep on Falcon-esque 13B for GTN slice. putting notes here for handoff.
jonathan: nice. what changed vs the last run?
sophia: briefly — product wants an explicit tradeoff call: which variant to surface in the beta, and a small blurb for GTN onboarding.
maya: summary: INT6 reduced token cost ~2.8x vs fp16, INT8 ~2.1x. quality delta (macro F1 on GTN slices) -> INT8: -0.9 pts, INT6: -2.6 pts. latency (p95) INT8 +12ms, INT6 +40ms.
lee: can you drop unit econ numbers? leadership wants cost per 1k tokens.
maya: sure — unit economics (approx): fp16 = $0.95 / 1k tokens; INT8 = $0.45 / 1k; INT6 = $0.34 / 1k. Those include packaging overhead (batching & KV cache).
jonathan: interesting. what's the priming hit-rate impact you mentioned earlier?
maya: priming hit-rate (fraction of requests that hit prefix cache for the template-heavy GTN traffic): fp16 62%, INT8 61%, INT6 58% — so INT6 lost more prefix matches due to truncated kv layout in our current INT6 kernel.
sophia: product risk note: GTN cares about hallucination on long contexts; did you measure hallucination drift?
maya: ran the hallucination probe 1k examples — hallucination increase: INT8 +0.7%, INT6 +1.9%. Confidence intervals small.
jonathan: thanks. any regression patterns by slot? (e.g., instructions vs factual QA)
maya: yes — INT6 shows concentrated drop on instruction-following prompts with long multi-turn history; INT8 mostly flat except for a tiny drop on numeric extraction.
lee: what's your chef score? (lol) — we asked for a single-line product-facing metric.
maya: ha. made one: Chef Score = (Quality_norm * 0.65) + (Latency_norm * 0.15) + (UnitCost_norm * 0.20) — higher is better. Normalization is relative to fp16 baseline.
ci-bot: automated test results: smoke e2e passed (all buckets), kvcache regression flag = 0.61, quant-kernel-oom = 0.
jonathan: what's the normalized table? paste sample.
maya: pasted below:
```
Variant | Quality_norm | Latency_norm | UnitCost_norm | ChefScore
fp16    | 1.00         | 1.00         | 1.00          | 1.00
INT8    | 0.987        | 1.012        | 1.895         | 0.987*0.65 + 1.012*0.15 + 1.895*0.2 = 1.14
INT6    | 0.974        | 1.042        | 2.794         | = 1.37
```
(note: we invert cost normalization so higher UnitCost_norm = more cost savings relative to fp16)
sophia: those chef numbers tilt strongly to INT6 because cost weight is high. product would worry about quality regressions. can we present a recommended default + fallback?
maya: recommendation for beta: default -> INT8 (balance). Fallback -> fp16 for any requests flagged by signal (long multi-turn or numeric-extraction). Keep INT6 off for now until kv-layout fix.
lee: agree. GTN wants the copy: "Default: INT8 for cost-effective throughput. For long-format or extraction-heavy queries, we route to fp16 to preserve fidelity."
jonathan: operational notes: enable canary with 5% traffic, route based on `slot_metadata.long_context==true || slot_metadata.task==\"extraction\"`. Also add a shadowing run on INT6 to collect more slices.
maya: created a canary flag in config: `quanter.canary.gtn_beta = 0.05`. pushed smoke dashboards: https://dash.redwood/boards/chef-gtn-quant
sophia: please add a short two-line blurb for GTN onboarding doc and a one-row scorecard.
maya: blurb + scorecard below: 
"Blurb: We recommend INT8 as the cost/quality sweet spot for GTN beta. Requests with long context or numeric extraction are routed to fp16 to avoid degradation. INT6 currently shows KV-cache and hallucination regressions; we keep it shadowed pending kernel fixes."
Scorecard: [Variant, DeltaCost, DeltaQuality(F1), Latency_p95_ms] -> INT8, -53%, -0.9pt, +12ms; INT6, -64%, -2.6pt, +40ms; fp16, 0%, 0pt, baseline.
lee: perfect. can you open a short PR to the GTN onboarding repo with these bullets?
maya: will do now. adding follow-up task: #TODO assign to runtime team for INT6 KV layout patch.
jonathan: thanks — nice crisp handoff. :thumbsup:
sophia: thanks all. we'll include recommendation in the GTN playbook.
ci-bot: note: nightly-run scheduled for 1756200000 to re-evaluate after microkernel push.
